expected.name: pool-wide-workload-identity-user-delta-with-condition
expected.why: The delta of this record carries an IAM condition object. The pattern reads the parts of one delta object with a skip that cannot pass a closing brace ([^}]*). With sorted keys the condition comes between action and the member and role, so the rule misses the grant. C19 tracks the correction: a skip that can pass one nested object. Not verified against a real record.

expected.name: aggregation-controller-writes-impersonate-users-into-admin
expected.why: The impersonate clause of sel_agg_beyond_builtin needs the keys of each RBAC rule in the order that the API server writes (verbs, apiGroups, resources). With sorted keys the rule misses the grant. K43 tracks the correction: one alternative for each key order.

expected.name: impersonate-system-masters-group-procB
expected.why: sel_priv_groups reads the group name with its JSON quotes ("system:masters"), so that a longer group name does not match. One element of a multi-valued field has no quotes. A store with such a field must test the element for equality. The rule as written is for a store that keeps the list as JSON text.

expected.name: in-pod-use-benign
expected.why: filter_incluster_last_source reads the last address of sourceIPs by the end of the list text ("]$), because a client can set each address but the last. A multi-valued field has no bracket and no last element that an item can name, so the filter does not hold and this in-cluster use fires. A store with such a field needs its own test of the last element. The rule as written is for a store that keeps the list as JSON text.

expected.name: smp-patch-uppercase-scheme
expected.why: The record holds an upper-case URL scheme (HTTPS://). The API server accepts it, and the attacker chooses the letter case. The item '"url": "http' matches it only where |contains ignores letter case, as Sigma specifies. A store whose match is case-sensitive needs a lower-case function on the field: no list of values can hold each mix of letter cases.

expected.name: scale-jsonpatch-replace-to-three
expected.why: filter_scale_jsonpatch_positive matches the whole operation list, from its first bracket (^\s*\[) to its last: one operation that sets a count above 0. One element of a multi-valued field is one operation without the brackets, so the filter does not hold and this scale to three fires. A store with such a field must test that the list holds that one operation only. The rule as written is for a store that keeps the list as JSON text.

expected.name: scale-smp-root-alias-retain-keys-with-count

The rule as written is for a store that keeps the list as JSON text.
